name: Hai Berden
status: Not an agent. Former chairman of Dutch club VVV-Venlo (2003–2018) and founder of Seacon Logistics. Returned as a co-owner of the club in early 2020.
summary: Dutch logistics businessman who, as chairman of small club VVV-Venlo, gave Keisuke Honda, Maya Yoshida and others their first step into European football. A 'gateway' person: he is the reason the Dutch door existed.
quick_facts: Founded Seacon Logistics in Venlo in 1985; about 500 employees in 2025
Sponsor from 1996, chairman 2003 to 2018, co-owner again from 2020
About 30 years of business ties with Japan (as of 2014)
Japanese players at VVV in his time
Keisuke Honda (2008), Maya Yoshida (2010), Robert Cullen (2011), Yuki Otsu (2012); coach Toshiya Fujita
Officer in the Order of Orange-Nassau (2018); a stand at the stadium is named after him

sections.title: In short
sections.intro: Berden is the answer to 'why Venlo?' He ran a shipping and warehouse company that did business with Japan, he also ran the local football club, and he joined the two. He asked a Dutch coach working in Japan for a talented player, got Honda, sold him for millions, and repeated the idea with Yoshida.

cells: Starts Seacon Logistics in Venlo. His idea: move containers from the sea port of Rotterdam to an inland hub. People called him crazy at first.
VVV-Venlo asks him to sponsor two business seats. The relationship grows from there.
The club is close to collapse. He becomes chairman and sets a goal: back in the top division by 2007.
His company becomes the stadium's name sponsor (2005) and the shirt sponsor (2007). VVV reach the top division in 2007.
On a business trip to Japan he asks Sef Vergoossen, a Dutchman from his region who is coaching Nagoya Grampus, for a Japanese talent. Vergoossen recommends Keisuke Honda.
Honda signs. VVV are relegated that spring, but Honda scores 16 goals the next season and they come straight back up.
Honda is sold to CSKA Moscow. Berden says the talks were long but constructive and the price was close to the club's target. He agrees to sign Yoshida, depending on that sale.
Yoshida, Cullen and Otsu follow. Yoshida is sold to Southampton in 2012.
Spends about two weeks in Japan, visits the injured Otsu, and tells a Japanese magazine about Honda and Yoshida. Former Japan player Toshiya Fujita is now a coach at VVV.
Made an Officer in the Order of Orange-Nassau, a Dutch royal honour, for his work in logistics and for the club.
Steps down after 15 years as chairman. The east stand is named the 'Hai Berden tribune'.
Returns as co-owner: he and eight other businessmen take 40% of the shares and invest €2 million. The club says this lets it work the Japanese market again.
Seacon returns as the stadium's name sponsor for 2025–26 and 2026–27.

sections.title: What he said about the Japanese players

rows: Honda: a very strong personality from the first meeting, which Berden credits for his success. He compared Honda's ambition and rebellious streak to Dutch legend Johan Cruyff.
https://number.bunshun.jp/articles/-/813731
He said he had never seen such a character at VVV.
https://www.vi.nl/nieuws/hoe-vvv-kennismaakte-met-een-onvergetelijk-japans-fenomeen
Yoshida: more of a 'typical Japanese' type than Honda. Serious, disciplined, responsible, and cheerful. Berden took him to a local pop concert when he arrived.
https://number.bunshun.jp/articles/-/813744
Otsu: Berden had followed him since his time at a German club and watched him at the London Olympics before signing him.
https://sportiva.shueisha.co.jp/clm/football/wfootball/2012/10/24/post_184/
Toshiya Fujita wrote that Berden's support let him stay at the club for three and a half years and become a coach, and that Berden came to his farewell match in Tokyo.
https://number.bunshun.jp/articles/-/830795

sections.title: Why it worked as a business

rows: Buy unknown, sell proven. Honda arrived as a 21-year-old few in Europe knew and left two years later for €6 million to €9 million, depending on the source.
https://www.voetbalzone.nl/nieuws/honda-vertrekt-voor-vier-jaar-naar-cska-moskou/93778
Yoshida was sold to Southampton for about £3 million.
https://www.goal.com/jp/%E3%83%8B%E3%83%A5%E3%83%BC%E3%82%B9/maya-yoshida-saints/blt22801bb776d61a11
The same man was chairman, main sponsor and stadium sponsor, so decisions were fast.
https://venlo.nieuws.nl/nieuws/21-inwoners-gemeente-venlo-gedecoreerd-tijdens-lintjesregen
Trust came from a coach who knew both worlds: a Dutchman from the same region, working in Japan.
https://www.vi.nl/nieuws/hoe-vvv-kennismaakte-met-een-onvergetelijk-japans-fenomeen
Care off the pitch: the club's staff greet Japanese visitors in Japanese, and a Japanese staff member worked there by 2014.
https://number.bunshun.jp/articles/-/813744

sections.title: Controversies and criticism
sections.intro: None found in this search (21 Nov 2026). The search for Berden was short, so this is not a full check.

rows: A gateway can be one person's hobby and business meeting. No federation plan or agent strategy created the Dutch route.
Small clubs are good first steps because the player plays every week. Honda even dropped to the second division and used it to grow.
The model later became an industry: Sint-Truiden in Belgium was bought by a Japanese company in 2017 to do on purpose what Venlo did by accident.

unverified: How his business ties with Japan began: not found. A Dutch magazine says the inland-container idea 'comes from Japan', but the meaning is unclear.
The fee VVV paid Nagoya for Honda: not found.
